## Historical audit — S0040

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2/results/smoke/fixed_h0/H0/smoke/commons_109923183/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 1 of 2 and no image pixels are available here.

| Evidence | Observation and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Student request, JSONL line 1 | The explicit goal was a separate-mesh reconstruction of one indoor photograph, including geometry, materials, viewpoint and framing. The student’s scene name and code imply an interpretation of a chaise in a paneled room; that interpretation is not independent confirmation of the photograph. |
| Student response line 3; execute step 1, line 4 | The program specified multiple scene elements: chaise, partial foreground chair, pillow, label, parquet, walls, window and curtains. It grouped chaise parts, positioned legs and rails, and rotated the head, wings and pillow. Grouping and coordinates do not verify physical connections, pose or image match. It also specified procedural fabric and bump materials, camera, lights and render settings; actual visible material appearance is unverified. |
| Execution result step 1, line 5; subsequent student request, line 6 | The first build failed at `world.use_nodes` because the scene world was `None`; its image was null. The runner supplied the traceback and requested a complete correction. This is execution feedback, not teacher instruction. |
| Student response line 8; execute step 2, line 9 | The student revised the program to create a world if absent, retaining substantially the same scene and camera/light setup. This is evidence of adopting the error feedback, not evidence of teacher advice. |
| Execution result step 2, line 10, characters [0,244771); select line 11 | The runner reported `ok: true`, saved a render and Blender scene, and selected step 2. The log shows 16 render samples, although the program requested 48. The successful execution does not establish visual or geometric correctness. |

**Outcome and limits.** The visible record supports a failed first execution followed by a formally successful second execution and selection—not an empty patch. Overall reconstruction quality, part contact, object visibility and occlusion, camera/framing accuracy, texture appearance and lighting remain unknown without the images. No visible teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, receipt or adoption is recorded in this chunk; no conclusion is drawn about the unseen chunk. The student sessions report zero tool calls (lines 2 and 7); the two generated programs and feedback-driven revision are the visible autonomous exploration, not evidence of broader search.

**Lessons and hypotheses.** Transferably, a runtime traceback can identify an environment initialization failure separately from scene-quality evaluation. Here, creating the missing world preceded a successful run; whether the intended named-mesh material assignments worked, and whether the selected composition matches the reference, remain unresolved task-specific hypotheses.
